analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the event. לְשִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים places it at the end of seven days, and the following clause states what happened: the floodwaters were upon the earth.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.

analysis.evidence: שִׁבְעַת counts הַיָּמִים, “the days.” The phrase לְשִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים means “after the seven days” and gives the time when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to שִׁבְעַת, the masculine singular construct form of the cardinal numeral.

analysis.evidence: In לְשִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים, the numeral שִׁבְעַת counts the seven days that elapsed before the floodwaters were on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural absolute noun.

draft.change: Amend the mabbul article to define the noun directly and cite Genesis 7:10 alongside Genesis 6:17 and Psalm 29:10.
draft.definition: A flood that overwhelms the land. In Genesis the noun names the deluge of Noah’s day.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:10 calls the waters upon the earth מֵי הַמַּבּוּל, “the waters of the flood.”

analysis.evidence: In וּמֵי הַמַּבּוּל, “and the waters of the flood,” מֵי is the construct form of “waters,” and הַמַּבּוּל identifies the flood to which they belong. The plural verb הָיוּ agrees with “waters,” which the verse says were upon the earth after seven days.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with the prefixed definite article הַ־, which doubles the initial מ. No suffix.
analysis.sense: The flood that covered the earth in Noah’s day.

analysis.evidence: מֵי הַמַּבּוּל means “the floodwaters,” and עַל הָאָרֶץ gives their location. הָיוּ links the two in the statement “the floodwaters were on the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, agreeing with the plural subject מֵי הַמַּבּוּל.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: In וּמֵי הַמַּבּוּל הָיוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל introduces the location of the floodwaters: they were on the earth.
הָיוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ says that the floodwaters were upon the earth. The phrase names the earth as the place reached by the flood, without specifying a particular territory.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הָ־.
